questions: Did the bruising and swelling begin after a blow, fall, accident, or other injury to your head or face?
Was the injury caused by another person?
Did you lose consciousness, become confused, or have a seizure?
Do you currently have a severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, unusual sleepiness, weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking?
Do you have blurred or double vision, loss of vision, severe eye pain, or pain when moving either eye?
Have you noticed clear fluid or blood coming from your nose or ears?
Did the swelling appear suddenly, or has it been rapidly worsening?
Do you have fever, redness, warmth, or severe tenderness around either eye?
Have you recently had facial or sinus surgery, dental surgery, or a severe sinus infection?
Are you taking blood thinners, aspirin, steroids, or medicines that increase bleeding?
Have you had unusual bruising or bleeding elsewhere, or a known bleeding disorder?
Have you recently eaten a new food, taken a new medication, or been exposed to something that could cause an allergic reaction?
Do you have swelling of your lips or tongue, difficulty breathing, or widespread hives?
Have you had similar unexplained bruising around your eyes before?
Do you have swelling in your legs, markedly reduced urine, or known kidney, liver, or heart disease?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Systemic AL (light-chain) amyloidosis from an occult plasma-cell dyscrasia, causing spontaneous bilateral periorbital purpura (“raccoon eyes”)

ALTERNATIVE: Acquired factor XIII deficiency

ALTERNATIVE: von Willebrand disease or another qualitative platelet-function disorder

ALTERNATIVE: Oculopalatal tremor or other acquired central vestibular disorder causing the isolated pendular torsional nystagmus, with unrelated periorbital purpura
